expectations.description: States that t-test on sum scores is not adequate without first testing measurement invariance
expectations.note: Clearly stated in opening and elaborated throughout — sum score t-test assumes measurement invariance which must be tested empirically.

expectations.description: Explains the configural → metric → scalar invariance sequence
expectations.note: All three levels explained with correct definitions: configural (same structure), metric (same loadings), scalar (same intercepts/thresholds).

expectations.description: Identifies scalar invariance as the level required for mean comparison
expectations.note: Explicitly stated: 'Scalar invariance — same item intercepts... This is the level you need for mean comparisons.'

expectations.description: Mentions partial scalar invariance as a fallback when full scalar fails
expectations.note: Dedicated section on partial scalar invariance as fallback, with guidance on how many intercepts should remain invariant (~80%+).

expectations.description: Names lavaan, semTools, measEq.syntax, or measurementInvariance function
expectations.note: Both lavaan and semTools named; measurementInvariance() function shown in code example; compareFit() also mentioned.

expectations.description: Mentions that ordinal/Likert items may need WLSMV estimator or threshold-based testing
expectations.note: Dedicated section on ordinal problem: polychoric correlations, WLSMV estimator, threshold parameters for invariance testing.

expectations.description: Either mentions PHQ-9 cross-cultural invariance issues specifically OR flags that translated mental-health scales commonly have invariance problems
expectations.note: Both: mentions published PHQ-9 cross-cultural studies showing partial invariance/factor structure differences, and notes somatic symptoms may map differently across cultural settings.

expectations.description: Does not greenlight a t-test on sum scores without invariance testing
expectations.note: Never recommends proceeding with t-test without invariance testing; bottom line explicitly states skipping invariance makes results 'uninterpretable.'
